description: If you're excited about wildfire detection, Earth observation data, or just want to build something meaningful with real NASA datasets, let's talk!
summary: NASA FIRMS publishes active-fire hotspots from MODIS (1 km, 2001→2026) and VIIRS (375 m, 2012→2026). Because VIIRS's pixels are finer, raw counts jump 2.3–4.9× at the 2012 sensor change — a fictional spike. FireLens measures the disagreement on the ~14-year overlap, calibrates VIIRS onto the MODIS scale with a per-region linear fit, and publishes one continuous "MODIS-equivalent" burning-activity calendar for five fire regimes (California, North India crop residue, Amazon, NSW, East Siberia). The pipeline processes 28.3M raw detections → 42,949 harmonized region-days → 6.9M cell-days. In-sample R² 0.90–0.95 for wildfire; North India crop burning is flagged at R² 0.59. Out-of-sample checks (leave-one-year-out, forward holdout) are committed alongside the fit. A React calendar app shows five views with CSV exports; a Leaflet map snaps drawn areas to the nearest precomputed region. All artifacts, validation, and a 28s demo video are open.
details:
Project Details:

What it does: Harmonizes MODIS + VIIRS active-fire archives into one continuous daily fire-cell count series (2001–30 Jun 2026) so year-over-year change reflects real fire activity, not the 2012 sensor swap.

How it works:

1. Clean FIRMS CSVs (confidence, FRP>0, drop volcano/offshore).

2. Grid both sensors onto identical H3 resolution-8 (~1 km) cells.

3. Fit OLS MODIS ~ a + b·VIIRS on overlap days per region; MODIS days keep measured values, gaps fall back to calibrated VIIRS.

4. Publish harmonized series + raw sensor series side-by-side for audit.

5. Calendar: weekly p10/median/p90 climatology, robust anomalies (value−median)/(p90−p10), per-year season start/peak/end, year×day heatmap.

Benefits / Impact:

- Responders compare current burning to consistent historical median.

- Scientists get an auditable, open MODIS-equivalent series (not an uncorrected splice).

- Land managers export CSV for their own tools.

- Honest limits: North India crop residue R² 0.59 (flagged), snapshot ends 30 Jun 2026, map snaps to 5 preset regions.

Tools / Languages:

Python 3.12 (pandas, NumPy, PyArrow, h3, FastAPI, requests), Node 20 (React 18, Vite, Leaflet), GitHub Actions CI, FFmpeg/Playwright for video.

Creativity:

- Correction measured on overlap, not assumed.

- Robust p10–p90 anomaly score means same thing in stable/volatile regions.

- All raw, calibrated, harmonized series stored together; validation JSON committed next to fit.

- Map explicitly labels "nearest preset" — no false custom-AOI promise.

Factors considered:

Sensor resolution difference, FRP vs cell-count divergence, crop-residue vs wildfire regimes, partial final year (2026), archive closure (S-NPP ended 1 Nov 2026), reproducibility for fresh clones.
